scoring_summary.passing: 6 pt passing TD (not standard 4), 25 yd/pt, -2 INT, +2 2pt conversion
scoring_summary.rushing_receiving: 10 yd/pt rush and rec, 6 pt TD, +2 2pt conversion
scoring_summary.kicker: Distance-based scoring: 0.1 pt per yard of made FG, no flat make bonus by distance bucket, no penalty for missed FG, +1 XP make / -1 XP miss
scoring_summary.defense: Heavy points-allowed scoring (10 pts shutout down to -4 for 35+ allowed), standard sack/INT/fumble/blocked kick/safety/TD scoring, plus a 4th-down-stop bonus

strategy_implications: 6-pt passing TDs modestly raise elite/rushing QB value even in a 1-QB format — don't need to reach round 1-2 for a QB, but a mobile high-TD passer can outkick his ADP.

Full PPR + only 1 FLEX means pass-catching RBs and high-target WRs/slot receivers carry a premium; touchdown-dependent players (goal-line backs, boom/bust deep threats) are slightly less valuable than pure PPR ADP suggests.
Kicker scoring rewards long-field-goal kickers over high-volume short-FG kickers — worth a very late-round look at distance rather than raw team scoring volume.
Defense scoring is boom/bust around points allowed — stream matchups against bad offenses rather than draft a 'name brand' defense early.
Only 1 bench-adjacent FLEX and 6 bench spots total in a 10-team league — depth still matters, but there's less room for pure lottery-ticket stashes than in deeper-bench leagues.
